newsitem.title: INDIA: India assesses typhoon devastation, death toll.
newsitem.headline: India assesses typhoon devastation, death toll.

text.p: Rescuers searched flooded coastal villages for survivors in the cyclone-hit southeastern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh on Friday amid growing official concern that more than 1,000 people may have died in storm.
Swathes of land in an area known as the rice bowl of Andhra Pradesh were submerged after torrential rain-lashed tidal waves surged up to five km (three miles) inland.

"I am at a loss for words to describe the tragedy in which about 1,000 people may have lost their lives," Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu was quoted as saying by the press Trust of India news agency.

Police and troops struggled through swirling floodwater up to three metres (10 feet) deep to reach many isolated coastal villages. Military helicopters dropped food packages and drinking water to the stranded, officials said.
"The momentum of the relief operation is building up now," said R.V. Chandravadan, a magistrate in Rajahmundry town, at the heart of the devastation.
Weather officials said the cyclone which struck on Wednesday night had dissipated as it moved inland.
Relief officials put the death toll at 477 late on Friday but expected it to rise.
Establishing accurate figures will be hard where whole villages were wiped out and tidal waters scattered bodies, officials said.
Few houses survived the combination of flood waters and winds gusting at more than 180 km per hour (110 mph).
State government spokesman Nageswara Rao put the number of homes destroyed or damaged in the deluge at 400,000 and said several thousand people had been injured.
In the East Godavari district, which was hit hardest, nearly 500 villages were inundated. The chief minister estimated losses at 20 billion rupees ($560 million) in the district.

Television pictures showed people wading waist deep through flood waters, overturned trucks, cars, uprooted trees strewn across roads and bodies trapped beneath trees which had crashed on to their fragile houses, while aerial shots showed large expanses of land under water.
"The rice bowl of the state looks like a burial ground," chief minister Naidu said after viewing the devastation.
The United News of India agency said seven people had been admitted to hospital with symptoms similar to cholera, as health workers faced a possible epidemic.
The seven were staying at a relief camp near Kakinada.

"There is no scare of an epidemic so far, medical teams are functioning well. However, power supply at many ares is still disrupted to a large extent," Varanasi Suryanarayana, a resident of Kakinada, told Reuters by telephone.
Around 3.5 million people live in the fertile Konaseema region around the Godavari river delta. Andhra Pradesh's flat coastline leaves it vulnerable to tropical storms coming from the Bay of Bengal.
In 1977, more than 10,000 people were killed by a cyclone that drove a tidal wave up to 12 km (eight miles) inland. A cyclone killed 120 people in June this year, and 967 people died in one in 1990.
